quiz.q: Why does the Commission's €45bn Ukraine plan for 2027 give a single country like Slovakia leverage?
options: Slovakia holds the Council presidency
It needs a change to the EU budget regulation, which requires unanimity
Slovakia would have to provide most of the money
Ukraine's loan is guaranteed only by Slovakia
quiz.explain: The money would be borrowed against EU budget headroom, so the budget regulation must be amended, and that needs all 27. [[p:Robert Fico]] says Slovakia will not take part, which is why the loan and the [[p:2028–34 budget|Multiannual Financial Framework]] talks are tangled together.

quiz.q: What did Hungary's decision on 20 Nov actually change for Ukraine and Moldova?
options: Both countries joined the EU single market
Screening reports for clusters 4 and 5 were approved, clearing a step before those clusters can open
Hungary agreed to fund Ukraine's 2027 budget
Accession talks were frozen until 2028
quiz.explain: Approving screening reports is a preparatory step. Opening the clusters still needs unanimous EU positions, possibly by the 15 Dec General Affairs Council.

quiz.q: Why did the drone strike on the Russian ship Sparta II worry Finland even though the ship was Russian?
options: It carried Finnish cargo
The burning ship drifted into Finnish waters, bringing the war's effects next to a NATO member's coast
Finland had leased the ship
It blocked Finland's only port
quiz.explain: Finland notified NATO allies and restricted sea and air traffic; PM [[p:Petteri Orpo]] said the war is spreading into neighbouring areas. Who launched the drones is an assessment, not confirmed.

quiz.q: What did the US–China–Russia meeting in Shenzhen produce on nuclear weapons?
options: A new trilateral arms-reduction treaty
A declaration repeating that nuclear war cannot be won, with dialogue but no limits or timeline
An agreement to resume nuclear testing
China's accession to New START
quiz.explain: The declaration restated a principle the five permanent Security Council members endorsed in 2022, and committed to talks on risk reduction without concrete limits.

quiz.q: Why are COP31 negotiators struggling over the final text?
options: The United States is blocking it from inside the room
Some states, reportedly including Saudi Arabia, resist any fossil-fuel language, while vulnerable countries refuse a text without it
The host country withdrew
There is no disagreement; only translation remains
quiz.explain: Drafts dropped explicit fossil-fuel wording and leaned on carbon removal. Panama threatened to object, and the talks ran into a second day of overtime in Antalya.
